title: The flat closed-fibre criterion for complete local rings
statement: Let $f:(A,\mathfrak m_A)\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$, with maximal ideal $\overline{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and its induced $k$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume $A$ and $B$ are complete for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Assume $f$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $\overline B$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\overline{\mathfrak m}$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. Then $B$ is formally smooth over $A$ for the $\mathfrak m_B$-adic topology.

source.place: Tag 07NQ (2) implies (3), complete-ring argument, from the compatible Cohen presentation through the final derivation correction; accessed at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07NQ and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07ED

proof.text: *Cohen presentation.* For the complete map, use [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-map-cohen-presentation] (Stacks 07NN): there is a commutative square $R\xrightarrow{u}S$, $R\twoheadrightarrow A$, $S\twoheadrightarrow B$, with $R,S$ complete regular local power-series rings over fields or Cohen rings, $u$ local and flat, and a regular system of parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $R$ whose images extend to one of $S$; in residue characteristic $p>0$ choose $t_1=p$. Put $\overline S=S/\mathfrak m_RS$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], $\overline S$ is regular local. The surjection $S\to B$ induces a surjection $\overline S\to\overline{B}:=B/\mathfrak m_{A}B$, since $R/\mathfrak m_R\cong A/\mathfrak m_{A}=k$ (the horizontal surjection is local).

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), diagram from Lemma Tag 07NN (lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings)

proof.text: *Remove the regular-fibre equations.* The complete closed fibre $\overline{B}$ is a Noetherian local quotient of $B$ by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure]. It is formally smooth over $k$ by hypothesis and therefore regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-geometrically-regular] (the trivial field extension gives regularity). The regular local surjection $\overline S\twoheadrightarrow\overline{B}$ has kernel generated by elements $\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r$ forming part of a regular system of parameters of $\overline S$, by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-kernel-parameters]. Lift each $\bar x_i$ to $x_i$ in the kernel of $S\twoheadrightarrow B$: a lift in $S$ maps to an element of $\mathfrak m_{A}B$, hence subtracting a suitable element of $\mathfrak m_RS$ makes it map to zero. In $\mathfrak m_S/\mathfrak m_S^2$, the classes of the $t_i$ are independent and the classes of the $x_i$ are independent modulo their span; hence all these classes are independent. Extend them to a basis and use Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] and [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension] to see that $t_1,\ldots,t_d,x_1,\ldots,x_r$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $S$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), paragraph beginning 'As B-bar and S-bar are regular'; Algebra Lemma Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular)

proof.text: Put $T=S/(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$. The map $S\to B$ factors through $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-parameter-quotient] (Stacks 07NM), $T$ is again a complete local power-series ring over the same kind of coefficient field or Cohen ring, with the images of $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ among its parameters (and $t_1=p$ in mixed characteristic). By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], these images form a regular sequence, so $R\to T$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular]. Its closed fibre $T/\mathfrak m_RT$ is $\overline S/(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_r)\cong\overline{B}$ as a local $k$-algebra, with the isomorphism induced by $T\to B$. It is formally smooth over $k$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology by transport of the lifting property [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), replacement of S by S/(x_1,...,x_r); Lemma Tag 07NM (lemma-quotient-power-series-ring-over-Cohen), Algebra Lemma Tag 07DY (lemma-flat-over-regular)

proof.text: *Identify the completed target with a base change.* The Cohen presentation in Step 2 gives a surjection $R\to A$. Let $D=T\otimes_R A\cong T/(\ker(R\to A))T$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change], and let $h:D\to B$ be induced by $T\to B$ and $A\to B$. It is surjective because $T\to B$ is. Both $D$ and $B$ are flat over $A$: $D$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] from $R\to T$ flat (Step 4), and $B$ by hypothesis. Modulo $\mathfrak m_{A}$, $h$ is the isomorphism $T/\mathfrak m_RT\to\overline{B}$ of Step 4. If $I=\ker h$, the exact sequence $0\to I\to D\to B\to0$ stays left exact after tensoring with $k$, because its last term is flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective]; the middle-to-last map is an isomorphism, so $I/\mathfrak m_{A}I=0$. The ring $D$ is a Noetherian local quotient of $T$ by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], so $I$ is finitely generated. Since $\mathfrak m_{A}D$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_D$, one has $I/\mathfrak m_D I=0$ as a quotient of $I/\mathfrak m_{A}I=0$. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] with the empty generating family gives $I=0$. Thus $h$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), displayed S tensor_R A -> B and following Nakayama argument; Algebra Lemmas Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero) and 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: *It remains to lift for $R\to T$.* If $T$ is formally smooth over $R$ for its maximal-ideal-adic topology, [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-base-change] gives the same for $D=T\otimes_R A$ over $A$ with the extended maximal ideal, which is the maximal ideal of $D$ since $D$ is a local quotient of $T$. Transport through $h:D\cong B$ (Step 5) gives formal smoothness of $B$ over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. We now prove the needed lifting property for $R\to T$ using its power-series coordinates. To lighten notation write $S=T$, let $\mathfrak m$ be its maximal ideal, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $K=S/\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), paragraph after S tensor_R A -> B, invoking Lemma Tag 07EG (lemma-base-change-fs)

proof.text: *Reduce a square-zero lifting problem to a residue-vector-space kernel.* Take an $R$-algebra $N$, a square-zero ideal $J\subseteq N$, and an $R$-algebra map $g:S\to N/J$ killing $\mathfrak m^n$ for some $n\ge1$ [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. The map $g$ makes $J$ an $S$-module: $s\cdot j$ is $g(s)j$, independent of a lift of $g(s)$ because $J^2=0$; thus $\mathfrak m^nJ=0$. Set $J_i=\{j\in J: \mathfrak m^i j=0\}$ for $0\le i\le n$. Then $0=J_0\subseteq J_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq J_n=J$, and $\mathfrak m(J_{i+1}/J_i)=0$. Each $J_i$ is an ideal of $N$, and each map $N/J_i\to N/J_{i+1}$ has square-zero kernel $J_{i+1}/J_i$. Therefore it suffices to solve the lifting problem for such a kernel, one quotient at a time. In that case $J$ is a $K$-vector space since $S/\mathfrak m=K$ is a field. Start from N/J_n and descend to N/J_0. A lift of a map killing m^e kills m^(2e), since its image of m^e lies in a square-zero kernel. Its action on the next kernel agrees with the original g-action because J²=0. Thus continuity and annihilation by m hold at every stage.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), final paragraph, filtration 0 subset J_1 subset ... subset J_n

proof.text: *An unrestricted lift, then correction of the parameter values.* Assume $\mathfrak mJ=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-fs-adic] (Stacks 07NL), $S$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ in residue characteristic zero and over $\mathbf Z$ in residue characteristic $p$. The original map $g$ and the map from the prime ring to $N$ form a lifting diagram for this property. In the characteristic-zero case, all nonzero integers are units in $N/J$ because $S$ contains $\mathbf Q$; a unit modulo a square-zero ideal is a unit in $N$ (if $ab=1+j$, inverse $1-j$ corrects it), so $N$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra as required. Hence obtain a ring map $\psi:S\to N$ lifting $g$. The coordinates of $S$ after Step 4 are formal variables $t_1,\ldots,t_d,y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over a coefficient field, or $t_2,\ldots,t_d,y_1,\ldots,y_m$ over a Cohen ring with $t_1=p$. For each $i$, $\psi(t_i)$ and the prescribed image $\varphi(t_i)$ of $R\to N$ differ by an element of $J$. Keep the coefficient-ring map fixed and substitute $\varphi(t_i)$ for $\psi(t_i)$: all variable images are nilpotent because $g(\mathfrak m^n)=0$ and $J^2=0$, so a formal series evaluates through a finite truncation. The resulting map still lifts $g$ and satisfies $\psi(t_i)=\varphi(t_i)$ for every $i$ (automatic for $p$).

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), final paragraph: lift by Lemma Tag 07NL, then change images of t_i by the universal property of power-series rings

proof.text: *The defect is a derivation from the residue field.* Since $\psi$ lifts $g$ and agrees with $\varphi:R\to N$ on $t_1,\ldots,t_d$, the difference $\Delta=\psi\circ u-\varphi:R\to J$ is additive, satisfies $\Delta(ab)=\varphi(a)\Delta(b)+\varphi(b)\Delta(a)$ (the product of two elements of $J$ is zero), and kills all $t_i$. By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], it corresponds to a linear map $\xi: \Omega_{R/\mathbf Z}\to J$. The $R$-action on $J$ factors through $k$ because $u(\mathfrak m_R)\subseteq\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak mJ=0$; hence $\xi$ kills $\mathfrak m_R\Omega_{R/\mathbf Z}$. It also kills $\mathrm dt_i$; these generate the image of $\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2$ in $k\otimes_R\Omega_{R/\mathbf Z}$ because the $t_i$ generate $\mathfrak m_R$. Exactness of the quotient differential sequence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] therefore makes $\xi$ factor uniquely through a $k$-linear map $\xi_0:\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\to J$. Tensor with $K$ to obtain a $K$-linear map $\xi_K:\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\otimes_kK\to J$.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07NQ, proof of (2) => (3), final paragraph, derivation D and factorization through Omega_{k/Z}; Algebra Lemma Tag 00RO (lemma-universal-omega) and Tag 00RU (lemma-differential-seq)

proof.text: *Extend and subtract the defect.* The closed fibre $\overline S=S/\mathfrak m_RS$ is formally smooth over $k$ (Step 4) and Noetherian local, so [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-field-differentials-injective] makes $\Omega_{k/\mathbf Z}\otimes_kK\to\Omega_{\overline S/\mathbf Z}\otimes_{\overline S}K$ injective. Extend $\xi_K$ to a $K$-linear map $\xi':\Omega_{\overline S/\mathbf Z}\otimes_{\overline S}K\to J$ by extending a basis of the image to a basis of the ambient vector space. Compose $S\to\overline S$, the universal derivation $\mathrm d:\overline S\to\Omega_{\overline S/\mathbf Z}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], reduction to $K$, and $\xi'$ to obtain a derivation $\Delta':S\to J$. For $r\in R$, its value equals $\xi_K(\mathrm d(r\bmod\mathfrak m_R)\otimes1)=\xi_0(\mathrm d(r\bmod\mathfrak m_R))=\Delta(r)$ by Step 9. Thus $\psi'=\psi-\Delta':S\to N$ is a ring homomorphism: additivity and unit are clear, and $\psi'(a)\psi'(b)=\psi(ab)-\psi(a)\Delta'(b)-\psi(b)\Delta'(a)$ since $J^2=0$, equal to $\psi(ab)-\Delta'(ab)$ by Leibniz. Also $\pi\psi'=g$ as $\Delta'$ lands in $J$, and $\psi'\circ u=\varphi$ by the equality of defects. This solves the residue-vector-space case of Step 7; induction along its filtration solves every square-zero lifting problem. Therefore $S$ is formally smooth over $R$ for its $\mathfrak m$-adic topology.
